newsitem.title: UK: Unionist leader says Blair meeting inconclusive.
newsitem.headline: Unionist leader says Blair meeting inconclusive.

text.p: David Trimble, leader of Northern Ireland's largest pro-British party, said on Monday his meeting with British Prime Minister Tony Blair about the "decommissioning" of IRA arms had not resolved the issue.
Speaking outside Blair's official London residence in Downing Street, Trimble said "there are some possibilities of progress...but the matter is not yet clear".

Trimble said that his party would be unable to support the government proposals in a crucial vote at the multi-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland on Wednesday unless the matter "has been sorted out" by then.
He was giving his initial reaction to the 45-minute meeting before holding a formal press conference at 1430 GMT.

One of the other pro-British parties in Northern Ireland has said it will boycott the multi-party talks because of the government's stance on when the IRA (Irish Republican Army) should have to give up its weapons.
The British government plans to invite the IRA's political arm, Sinn Fein, to take part in the talks from September following the guerrilla group's declaration of a ceasefire at the weekend.
